title: Codebook-Guided Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for Structurally Heterogeneous Features
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Distill across mismatched feature structures by routing teacher knowledge through a selected shared codebook instead of aligning features unit by unit.
layout: Single wide panel, two mirrored branches left-to-right, vertical loss arrow on right
description: A single wide diagram with two horizontal branches. The top branch is the teacher: a dog video frame goes to a locked Image Encoder, then to a 3D intermediate feature block. From there it splits to the original task head and to a projection that produces a colorful quantized feature block, which feeds a codebook-branch task head and then a prediction q(t). The bottom branch is the student: an audio waveform goes to an Audio Encoder, a feature block, a projection, and a quantized feature, then a blue codebook-branch head and predictions q(s) and p(s). On the left, a teacher-side codebook feeds an 'Important Code Selection' box. That box feeds a smaller student-side codebook. Yellow arrows mark the codebook, commitment and prediction-matching losses. Green is the teacher, blue is the student, and gold is the losses and codes. Lock icons mark frozen modules. A true label y feeds the task losses.
caption: Overview of the proposed framework. We learn a teacher-side vector-quantized codebook (Sec. [ref]), select task-relevant and student-compatible codes (Sec. [ref]), and use the selected codes for student-side distillation (Sec. [ref]). The framework enables feature-level CMKD without requiring explicit unit-level correspondence between structurally different teacher and student representations.
abstract: Cross-modal knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a teacher modality to a student modality. Existing feature-level alignment methods typically assume that teacher and student features reside in structurally alignable representation spaces. However, this assumption does not hold when cross-modal features are structurally heterogeneous and lack clear unit-level correspondence, such as 2D spatial visual grids and 1D temporal audio sequences, thereby limiting the applicability of feature-level alignment. To address this challenge, we propose a cross-modal distillation framework that enables effective knowledge transfer across structurally heterogeneous feature spaces via a vector-quantized codebook. Specifically, teacher features are abstracted into a set of vector-form codes regardless of their original feature structure, and the selected codes serve as concept-level anchors for student learning. Code selection is guided by both task relevance and student compatibility, allowing the student to receive transferable teacher knowledge without requiring direct unit-level feature alignment. Experimental results across diverse cross-modal distillation scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on classification and semantic segmentation tasks.
